headline: What to Include in a Homeschool Portfolio: The Five Core Contents
sub: A typical portfolio holds these five things.
items: A log of educational activities, with reading materials named by title.
Samples of work across the year, dated, from more than one point rather than one good week.
A list of subjects covered and the materials or curriculum used.
Attendance or days schooled, where your state counts them.
Test results or an evaluator's written report, where required.

headline: Homeschool Evaluation Prep: Get Ready in One Evening, Step by Step
sub: This assumes you already have work sitting around the house.
items: First 15 minutes: Confirm with your evaluator: meeting time, location, and anything specific they want to see.
Next 20 minutes: Pull one dated work sample per subject from early in the year and one from recently.
Next 15 minutes: Write a subject and curriculum list, one line each.
Next 15 minutes: Add a short note per subject: what changed, what was hard, what you'd do differently.
Last 10 minutes: Put it all in one folder, in the order your evaluator will likely go through it.

headline: What to Keep per Subject in a Homeschool Portfolio
sub: A rough guide. Adjust to what your state and your evaluator ask for.
items: Math: Worked problems showing the method, not just the answer (A few pieces per term)
Writing: A first draft and the finished version of the same piece (Two or three per year)
Reading: A running list of books, finished and abandoned (Ongoing)
Science: Photos of experiments, plus what was concluded (Per topic)
History and geography: Anything with a date and an argument in it (Per topic)
Art and practical subjects: Photos, since the work itself rarely fits in a folder (As produced)

a photo of a volcano model with a caption she dictated
a running list of eleven books read or abandoned since school started

headline: Homeschool Evaluation: What to Bring to the Meeting, a Six-Item Folder List
sub: Ask your own evaluator or state what it requires.
items: The log of what was covered, with dates, even if approximate.
Work samples from more than one point in the year, not just one strong stretch.
A list of curricula and materials used.
Attendance or days schooled, if your state counts them.
Test results, if your state requires them.
A short note per subject on where you started and where you got to.
